title: Reactivity Training
summary: Build confidence and safer responses to everyday triggers using positive reinforcement, comfortable distances and gradual practice.

subcategories.title: Building Positive Associations with Triggers
subcategories.goal: Help the dog feel safer when seeing something that worries them.
subcategories.steps: Begin far enough from the trigger that the dog remains comfortable. When the trigger appears, offer small, high-value treats. Stop feeding when it disappears. Keep repetitions brief and increase distance if the dog becomes tense.
subcategories.coachingNotes: Do not require eye contact or obedience before feeding. The aim is to change the emotional association. Avoid deliberately provoking a reaction.

subcategories.title: Calm Reward Delivery
subcategories.goal: Deliver food rewards in ways that support relaxed, comfortable behaviour.
subcategories.steps: Practise predictable, gentle treat delivery in a quiet location first. Observe how the dog responds to your hand movements, reward placement and pace. Use the approach that helps them remain comfortable before introducing mild distractions.
subcategories.coachingNotes: Avoid reaching over a worried dog or making sudden movements. Adjust your delivery to the individual dog; excitement around food does not necessarily indicate relaxation.

subcategories.title: Let's Go — Moving Away Together
subcategories.goal: Teach a positive cue for turning and moving away from a difficult situation.
subcategories.steps: Start without distractions. Say 'Let's go', turn gently and reward the dog for following. Practise in both directions. Once familiar, use the cue early when you notice a potential trigger and reward movement away.
subcategories.coachingNotes: Keep the lead relaxed and avoid jerking the dog around. Practise frequently in easy situations so the cue predicts a rewarding activity.

subcategories.title: Staying Comfortable Around Dogs and People on Walks
subcategories.goal: Build calmer responses to everyday triggers during walks.
subcategories.steps: Choose quiet locations with room to create distance. Reward comfortable observations and voluntary reconnection with you. Use short sessions and gradually introduce more challenging environments as the dog becomes ready.
subcategories.coachingNotes: Watch for tension, prolonged staring or difficulty disengaging. These indicate that the situation may be too demanding. Increase distance rather than correcting barking.

subcategories.title: Confidence During Everyday Encounters
subcategories.goal: Help the dog cope when the handler pauses or interacts with other people.
subcategories.steps: Arrange brief, predictable encounters with a helper who stays at a comfortable distance. Reward the dog during the encounter and allow space to move away. Gradually increase the interaction's duration while monitoring their comfort.
subcategories.coachingNotes: Ask helpers to avoid approaching, staring at or reaching towards the dog. Let the dog choose whether to approach; greetings are optional.
